title: Experiment Noise Detection & On-Call Playbook (wip)
summary: Practical, cross-functional runbook for detecting experiment signal vs noise and for on-call reaction patterns when A/B or staged exposures begin producing noisy metrics. Focused on LLM features (generation, rerank, embeddings) but intentionally model-agnostic.
audience: Experiment owners, product stewards, SRE/on-call, data science, ML infra. Primary readers: experiment steward + oncall responder.
scope: Covers detection heuristics, minimal dashboards and alert thresholds, notification templates, escalation steps, immediate rollback/flighting actions, quick postmortem notes. Does NOT replace full incident runbook — this is experiment-specific guidance.
background: We run progressive exposures for model changes and feature flags. Small metric variance is normal; sometimes transient noise mimics a regression and triggers unnecessary rollbacks. This doc codifies a pragmatic way to separate benign noise from real user-impacting regressions and to reduce churn from premature rollbacks.
quick-runbook:
1) Triage start: who gets paged? -> primary experiment steward + oncall.
2) Surface: look at source metrics (latency, error-rate, model-confidence proxies, cost burn, user-facing quality signals).
3) Windowing: compare 1h/6h/24h windows and check segment overlap (new cohorts vs baseline).
4) Canary guard: is impact concentrated on <1% of traffic or a specific geo/device? If yes, consider throttling exposure rather than full rollback.
5) Action: one of {hold traffic, throttle by factor of 2, flip to stable variant, rollback}. Document which action taken in the experiment ticket.
6) Notify: send templated message to experiment channel and stakeholders (see notification-actions).
7) Follow-up: schedule short postmortem if action was more than throttling or if user-facing impact observed.
detection-rules: Signal: sustained degradation in primary KPI for >30m AND outside historical daily variation (z-score > 2).
Noise: single-spike in a derived metric without corroborating signals (no change in latency or errors) — label as investigate but do not rollback immediately.
Credible-impact rule: at least two orthogonal signals (e.g., user conversion drop + increased hallucination complaints + higher token cost) before automated rollback.
Cohort isolation: if a metric change is only in a microcohort <0.5% of traffic, automatically throttle that cohort and observe for 60–120 min.
dashboard-panels: Experiment overview: current exposure fraction, cohort breakdown, recent changes (model version, prompt template).
Primary KPI time-series: 1m/5m/60m aggregation toggles. Include baseline cohort overlay.
Quality signals: sampled QA failure rate, user complaint rate, classification confidence proxies.
Synthetic probes: golden prompts pass/fail and distribution of outputs by similarity to expected set.
notification-actions: Pager message (urgent): short subject 'EXP: <exper_id> KPI degradation' + 3-line summary + immediate action taken + link to ticket + link to dashboard.
Experiment Slack channel: longer context in #prod-experiments including sample problematic output and cohort ids. Tag product steward, SRE, data-science.
Email to stakeholders (if impacting >5% of paying users): timeline summary + mitigation plan + expected next update time.
escalation-matrix: Level 0: steward & oncall react, possible throttle (no exec notif). Level 1: cross-functional sync within 30m if impact persists >60m or affects >1% traffic; include product, SRE, ML infra, DS. Level 2: exec pager and potential customer comms if >5% paying-user impact or SLA breach. Always record decisions in the experiment ticket and update the channel every 30–60 minutes until stabilized.
operational-automation:
Short automations to implement: 
- cohort throttle playbook: API to reduce exposure by factor N and confirm health after 30m.
- automated noise classifier: flag alerts as 'likely noise' if only one metric and no error/latency signals.
- synthetic probe runner: run golden prompts every 5m and fail experiment if >X consecutive failures.

postmortem-template: 1) What happened (1 paragraph). 2) Timeline with ticks (when exposure changed, when alerts fired, actions taken). 3) Root cause hypotheses and evidence. 4) Why automation or detectors missed it (if applicable). 5) Action items (owner + ETA). 6) Communication summary for customers (if needed).
open-questions: What thresholds should we set for model-quality proxies (similarity metrics) — DS to propose candidate values by 2025-02-14.
Should synthetic probes be single golden prompt or a small suite? (tradeoff: coverage vs flakiness).
Edge case: experiments affecting personalization vectors — how do we reconstruct baseline quickly?
Do we allow automated rollbacks for small revenue-impact experiments? (policy decision from PL).
